claims.statement: A closed five-hop transaction cycle exists returning funds to the originating account: ACCT-2054 -> ACCT-2055 -> ACCT-2056 -> ACCT-2057 -> ACCT-2058 -> ACCT-2054, indicating round-tripping rather than legitimate commerce.
The cycle closes back to ACCT-2054 via TXN-0067, confirming funds returned to point of origin.
All five hops occur within a 24-hour window (2026-07-12T09:00 to 2026-07-13T09:00), satisfying the short time-window criterion for coordinated circular movement (RT-2).
Hop amounts range from $25,068.90 to $26,722.01, varying by less than 25% across all five transactions, consistent with layering designed to preserve value while obscuring origin (RT-3).
Each account in the cycle triggered an individual circular fund flow alert, corroborating system-level detection of the round-tripping pattern across all five participants.
ACCT-2056 alert independently flags the same cyclical structure at the midpoint of the chain.
ACCT-2057 alert confirms circular flow involvement at the second-to-last hop.
ACCT-2055 alert confirms circular flow involvement at the first receiving hop.
ACCT-2058 alert confirms circular flow involvement at the final hop before funds return to origin.

None of the five personal accounts have any KYC notes on file, and none display an occupation or income profile (Homemaker, Retired, Student) that would economically justify sequential transfers of ~$25,000-$26,700 each within hours, undermining any legitimate business rationale for the fund movement.

content.summary: The five accounts (ACCT-2054 through ACCT-2058) form a closed, rapid, same-magnitude transaction loop that returns funds to the originating account within 24 hours, meeting all three standardized round-tripping criteria (cyclical flow, short time window, similar hop amounts). Each account independently triggered a circular fund flow alert, and none of the account holders' profiles (homemakers, a retiree, and students with modest declared incomes) provide plausible economic justification for sequential transfers of $25K-$27K each. The absence of any KYC documentation across all five accounts further compounds the risk, strongly supporting a determination of suspicious round-tripping activity consistent with layering to obscure fund origin or manufacture transaction history.
